context_notes: This session resumed a paused Phase 11 via /gsd:resume-work, completed 2 scoped follow-ups (scheduler resource-kind hardcoding across 3 files; CI-scoping via multi_node marker + staggered monitoring stack), both fully verified working via live CI. Then opened a debug session for a deeper, previously-uninvestigated issue: no DAG has EVER been observed reaching SUCCEEDED on GitHub's CI runners. Found a real, well-evidenced root cause (scheduler/dag-processor crash-looping because Airflow's internal scheduler_health_check_threshold/dag_file_processor_timeout are tighter than the K8s probe timeoutSeconds that was raised in an earlier session). Verified the fix offline against the project's own authoritative CPU-budget policy gate (test_ci_profile_fits_runner passes), pushed it, then used a throwaway PR to get direct live restart-count evidence. Result: partial success -- scheduler is fixed, dag-processor is not. This is genuinely unresolved, not a false-confidence stopping point. Two unrelated, pre-existing CI flakes were also discovered along the way and documented but NOT chased (out of scope): a Kyverno admission-webhook self-timeout during cluster-up, and a vault-0 pod-not-found race in scripts/stages/80-vault.sh's own post-install wait logic.
